b.The Bel voir Ranch was purchased by the City of Cheyenne in
response to the need to site a new landfill and develop ground water resources.
(A landfill will not be placed on the Bel voir Ranch for the foreseeable future
since expansion of the current landfill has been approved.)While
development of groundwater resources is a future development(potentially
years away), City investigative work could be ongoing on ranch property.
These activities by the City and/orits agentswill have priority for land use.
Very little impact is anticipated to the grazing opportunities.
c.A wind power developer(NEXTERA ENERGY Resources)holds alease to

construction and placement of wind towers, transmission facilities, andaccess
roads.If the developer exercises this lease, this grazing lease will be
renegotiated to accommodate this development.
d.Portions of the Ranch may be developed for non-motorized recreational
activity.This would most likely take place in the southwestern portion ofthe
Ranchand consist of a trail from the State section adjacent to Harriman Road
to the“Big Hole.”Minimal impact on grazing is anticipated; however, the
grazing leasemay be renegotiated to accommodate this development.

3.Rental.Annual rental for this Lease shall be in the amount of $187.477.50 which
rental shall be payable as follows:
a.The sum of $93.738.75 shall be due and payable upon stock arrival or
before June 15, each year. (1/2 of total, adjusted as necessary to reflect actual
number (head) of stock allowed).
b.The remaining sum of $93.738.75 (1/2 of total amount) shall be due
and payable upon stock removal or before October31, each year.
c.Annual Rental is based on a standard of1,050 AUMs for five months at $35.71
per AUM ($25.00 per yearling).
d.The Lessee will graze and pay for a minimum of 1,050 AUMs (1,500
yearlings) for 5 months unless the City determines a lower number or
timeframe based on the condition of the pasture.Lessee will payfor actual use
determined byAUM and time ontherange.
e.Lessor shall pay state leasefees and anyreal and personal property taxes
which are assessed against the Leased Premises during the term of this
Lease, and all water assessments, fees and related charges.
f.Lessee shall pay any personal property taxes with respect to Lessee's
personal propertyand chattels.In addition, Lessee shall pay all expenses
normally associated with grazing operations incurred by Lessee in
connection with its use of the Leased Premises.
4.Ranching Methods. Lessee shall use the Leased Premises for grazing and
related purposes only.Lessee agrees to follow the best grazing, ranching, and
husbanding practices prevailing and shall operate the Leased Premises in
good, first class, and workmanlike manner in such a way as to not damage or
harm the grass plants growing thereon by over grazing.Lessor shall bear the
expense of chemicals for spraying of noxious weeds and shall be responsible
for all spraying and application costs. Lessee shall conduct all of its
operations on the Leased Premises in full compliance with all applicable
federal, state or local laws, rules regulations and ordinances.
5.General Stipulations.
a.Summer grazing normally allowed May through October depending on
range conditions except as otherwise mutually agreed in writing by both
parties.
4:
b.Range conditions permitting, no more than approximately1,540AUMs
total will be allowed on the property. This number could be less depending
onrange andwater availability.
c.Pasture rotation will follow a time frame as established bythe Lessor in
consultation with the Laramie County Conservation District.Livestock
will not be allowed to be split between pastures or moved between
pastures without the express permission of the Lessor through the Ranch
Manager.
d.It is the sole responsibility of the Lessee to monitor and move cattle as
required. The Ranch Manager will provide oversight only.
e.Veterinary care, medicines, and supplies and any salt or minerals will
be the responsibility of the Lessee.
f.The Lessor will not be responsible for any“death loss".
g.Lessor will provide the infrastructure (wells, generators, piping, tanks,
etc.)to supply water.However, it is the Lessee's responsibility to fuel
generators and ensure availability of water to cattle.If there is a problem
with the water infrastructure, the Lessee should notify the City and take
interim action to provide livestock with water until the infrastructure can
berepaired by the City.Damage to water infrastructure (tanks, etc),
caused bylivestock, will be the responsibility of the Lessee.
h.Maintenance ofcorrals, fences, and any other ranch facilities relating to
grazing operations will be the responsibility of the Lessee.This includes
providing fencing materials.Lessee is responsible for full repair of any
damage caused to ranch facilities or infrastructure by Lessee's operations.
Access to property will be provided a least 30 days prior to stock arrival
for site preparation. Gates will be kept closed at all times.
i.Irrigated pastures near the ranch headquarters are not included in
this lease.These excluded pastures are identified as all or part of CIN
13,14,15,16,17 on the attached Pasture Map.
j.Up to six(6) saddle horses can be kept on the premises during the lease
period. Care of stock will be the responsibility of the Lessee. Lessee may
operate ATVs for cattle management. Lessee assumes all liability related
to such activities.
k.All dates of use, pasture locations, and maximum numbers of head of
stockwill be determined by the Lessor.The decisions will bebased on
range conditions at the time.Lessor reserves theright to determine,
under any contingent circumstances (such as flood, fire, drought, etc.),
when and how many head of stock the range can carry atanygiven
time and reserves the right to require immediate reduction orremoval
of livestockto those numbers deemed appropriate by the Lessor.
